title: Seedlings Lean for More Than One Reason

# Seedlings Lean for More Than One Reason

A tray bending toward the window often needs more even light, but a weak stem can also come from crowding, excessive warmth, or roots kept constantly wet. Rotating the tray hides the direction for a day without fixing the cause.

## Compare growth, not only angle

Measure the distance between leaves, note stem thickness, and inspect whether all varieties lean equally. Long pale stems suggest insufficient light; a single collapsing patch may indicate damping-off or uneven moisture. Move lights gradually closer while checking leaf temperature.

## Add gentle movement

Air circulation reduces stagnant humidity and encourages sturdier stems, but a fan should not dry tiny cells within an hour. Short, indirect airflow is enough. Thin crowded seedlings so leaves do not overlap and compete.

Water observations from [[06-soil-watering|Reading Soil Moisture Before Watering]] help distinguish light-seeking growth from root stress.
